items.headline: Anthropic's Biggest Threat Report Yet: How Criminals Are Misusing Claude, and What They Stole
items.summary: Anthropic published its most detailed threat intelligence report to date, covering nine months of misuse it found and shut down, cyberattacks, scams, propaganda campaigns, and even research that could help build weapons. A recurring pattern stood out: attackers who got into someone's AI setup weren't after the AI itself, they were after stolen API keys (the password-like codes that let apps and automations talk to Claude on your behalf) so they could rack up usage on someone else's account or dig further into connected systems.
items.why_it_matters: If you've ever pasted an API key into an automation tool (like n8n or a custom script) to connect Claude to your business, treat that key like a spare house key: don't share it, don't hard-code it into a public file, and rotate it if you ever suspect it leaked.

items.headline: Apple Confirms the New AI-Powered Siri Arrives This Month
items.summary: Apple confirmed its long-awaited overhaul of Siri, internally branded 'Siri AI,' will roll out in English with iOS 27 on September 14, with five more languages following in October. The new Siri gets its own standalone app, can hold real back-and-forth conversations, understands what's on your screen or in a photo, and can take actions inside apps like Messages and Reminders based on what you're doing in the moment.
items.why_it_matters: This is the update that finally brings Apple's assistant closer to what Claude or ChatGPT can already do, worth a look the week it lands since most of your audience will have it on their iPhone whether they ask for it or not.

opportunity.angle: I tested the new AI Siri the day it landed on iOS 27, here's what it actually gets right (and wrong)

items.headline: California Becomes First State to License Independent AI Auditors
items.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom signed a new law creating the nation's first state registry of independent AI auditors, people and firms certified to check AI companies' safety and bias claims instead of AI companies grading their own homework. The registry itself won't be up and running until 2029, but it sets the direction: outside verification of AI safety claims is coming.
items.why_it_matters: You don't need to do anything about this one, but it's an early sign that 'independently verified' AI claims may become a real selling point, worth remembering the next time a tool's marketing leans hard on unverified safety promises.

items.headline: Adobe Stuffs Five AI Video Generators Right Into Premiere Pro's Timeline
items.summary: Adobe released a big AI update for Premiere Pro that lets you draw a blank spot on your timeline, describe what you want, and generate it without leaving the app, with a choice of Adobe's own Firefly model or partner models from Google Veo, Runway, Kling, or Luma. The same update adds in-timeline AI sound effects, music, and soundscape generation, plus an AI assistant inside After Effects.
items.why_it_matters: This is Adobe's answer to the kind of AI-assisted editing DaVinci Resolve has been building toward, worth a look even if you're a Resolve loyalist since it shows where AI video generation inside a real editor (not a separate app) is heading.

opportunity.angle: I tried generating video and sound right inside Premiere's timeline so you don't have to switch apps

items.headline: Notion Just Switched Off Its Premium AI Models By Default
items.summary: Starting September 10, Notion turned premium AI models (the more capable, higher-cost options) off by default for Notion Agent in every workspace. A workspace owner or admin now has to manually turn one on in Settings before anyone on the team can use it, and doing so spends Notion credits, which are billed separately.
items.why_it_matters: If you or your team uses Notion's AI features, this could quietly make Notion Agent feel dumber overnight, worth checking your workspace settings if AI answers suddenly seem off, you may just need an admin to flip premium models back on.

opportunity.action_note: If you use Notion Agent for your business, check Settings → Notion AI this week and turn premium models back on if your answers have gotten noticeably worse since September 10.

items.headline: Old YouTube Studio App Versions Stopped Working This Week
items.summary: YouTube confirmed that Studio mobile app versions 24.31.6 and earlier are no longer supported as of September 9. If your phone hasn't auto-updated the app recently, features may break or stop loading until you grab the latest version from the App Store or Play Store.
items.why_it_matters: A quick, boring, two-minute fix: if your YouTube Studio app has been acting glitchy on your phone this week, this is almost certainly why, update it before you assume something bigger is wrong.

opportunity.action_note: Open the App Store or Play Store on your phone right now and update the YouTube Studio app so you don't lose access mid-upload.
